Hello eveyone! I hope you are doing ok!

 

It's been a while but I have finally managed to get on with reworking how I code my website and updating some parts to make things easier for me. I posted update with my rss feed I use for website updates but I wanted to make a blog post as well talking about it a bit more ( and to also test that my blog rss is working too).

 

I learned how to use eleventy, which makes coding my website a lot easier! I used petrapixel's eleventy tutorial. It was easy installing everything but setting up the templates for my website and getting it all to work right was difficult. Once I got it working though it was all good! I should be able to make pages much quicker now. There was also a webpack tutorial which should allow me to use one javascript file and one css file instead of using a whole bunch, but I didn't think it would matter to me since I'm using eleventy anyway and also I had some javascript files that I only wanted running on certain pages and wasn't sure how that would work if everything was in one file.

 

I also switched to a new blog template using Zonelets. I was also having a hard time getting things to work with my website structure. I had to adjust the template script for my needs. When getting it to work with eleventy, the date part of the blog post pages kept getting deleted when I ran the elventy script. I had to adjust the post format variable in the blog script so that it won't happen. So my nunjucks files containing the code for each of my blog posts have commas instead of where the dashes should be. I tried to see if there was a way to turn off this behavior for eleventy but I couldn't find a solution so this was the alternative I came up with. I was so confused as to the links to the pages weren't working until I noticed the issue XD.

 

I recomend using Zonelets with eleventy becuase the ability to create and reuse templates to create the pages for each blog post is so helpful!

 

Another addition is that I added an rss feed to my blog so that others who subcribe to the feed would be notified of any new posts I make. I thought I could only have one rss feed but then I learned I could have more. So now, I'll keep my website updates on one feed, and my blog posts in another.

 

While trying to set up my blog, I found a way to style my rss feeds so now they look pretty! I won't need to use the update window anymore. I'm suprized that this wasn't mentiond in the rss tutorials I found. I ended up linking a tutorial on how to style it on the rss feed page itself. I'll link my rss stylesheet so others can take a look and modify it for thier rss feeds. I was confused on how it worked until I realized the rss stylesheet is like coding in html (but with extra stuff). I would then link a seperate css file for the styling, same way you would in a regular html file.

 

I really love the way it turned out!
